title: Cattle Herd Health & Vaccination Schedule
desc: Comprehensive South African regional livestock health master manual detailing growth stages, seasonal timelines, clostridial/botulism protocols, and parasite management.
steps: Newborn Calves (0-3 Months): Administer navel disinfection with iodine on Day 1. Ensure colostrum intake within the first 6 hours. Perform ear tagging, dehorning, and castration at 1 to 3 months. Give initial Clostridial (3-in-1 / 5-in-1) and Botulism vaccinations at 3 months, followed by a booster 4 weeks later.

Weaners & Growing Stock (4-12 Months - Pre-Winter): Administer mandatory Brucellosis (S19 or RB51) vaccination to all heifer calves between 4 and 8 months. Complete clostridial booster shots before weaning stress. Implement targeted internal deworming and regional tick control.

Adult Breeding Herd - Spring (Sep-Nov / Pre-Calving): Administer annual booster vaccinations for Botulism (Lamsiekte), Clostridial diseases, and reproductive tract infections (Vibriosis/Trichomoniasis) 6 weeks prior to the breeding season.

Summer & Wet Season (Dec-Apr / Peak Tick & Parasite Risk): Apply regular acaricide dip or pour-on rotation to combat vectors of Redwater, Anaplasmosis (Galsiekte), and Heartwater. Monitor calves closely for tick-borne diseases and administer corrective treatments.

Winter & Dry Season (May-Aug / Nutritional Maintenance): Provide appropriate phosphate/protein licks or winter energy supplements. Conduct bull breeding soundness evaluations (sperm motility and physical exams) 6 weeks prior to joining.

title: Poultry Brooder Setup & Management
desc: Temperature regulation, lighting programs, and biosecurity protocols for day-old chicks.
steps: Pre-heat brooding house 24-48 hours before and verify floor temperature (30-32°C) with an infrared scan.
Set up chick guards with a circular boundary (min. 2.4m diam.) and eliminate sharp corners and drafty pockets.
Provide fresh water by cleaning, disinfecting, and flushing lines, and positioning founts, bell drinkers, and nipple lines correctly.
Monitor temperatures by observing chick behavior to identify comfort zones, calibrate sensors, and log data.

title: Sheet Metal Cone Fabrication Guide
desc: Step-by-step master guide for calculating sector angles, marking patterns, cutting, forming, and joining a sheet metal cone.
steps: Step 1: Calculate Sector Angle (θ) - Calculate θ = 360° × (r / R) where r is the base radius and R is the slant radius.
Step 2: Draw the Pattern on Sheet Metal - Use a trammel set to radius R from apex point O, mark angle θ with a protractor, and add a 10-15mm lap allowance.
Step 3: Cutting & Surface Prep - Cut out the pattern using snips, deburr sharp edges with a file, and pre-bend the lap allowance.
Step 4: Forming the Cone - Form the cone either by using a rolling machine (Option A) or manually working the sheet over a pipe stake (Option B).
Step 5: Joining the Seam - Align edges, clamp securely, and join using a TIG torch (tack welding top/bottom first) or a rivet gun.

title: Foundation Squaring & Layout Guide
desc: Step-by-step master guide for accurately laying out building lines, establishing baselines, applying the 3-4-5 rule for right angles, squaring walls, cross-measuring diagonals, and setting up batter boards.
steps: Establish the Baseline: Drive Peg A into the ground, run a mason's line to Peg B, and measure/mark Corner B along the line.
Apply the 3-4-5 Rule: Mark 3 units on the baseline from Corner A (Point X), measure 4 units outward, and measure a 5-unit hypotenuse from Point X to intersect the 4-unit line to drive Peg C.
Extend and Square the Second Wall: Line up string from Corner A through Peg C, extend the string to the full required length, and mark Corner D.

Verify and Secure Layout: Cross-measure diagonals A-D and B-C, adjust pegs until they match completely, build secure batter boards outside the footprint, transfer exact string lines to notches, and remove pegs to dig.

title: Concrete Foundation Pouring & Curing
desc: Comprehensive technical master guide for professional concrete foundation pouring, trench preparation, formwork bracing, rebar chair spacing, mix ratios, vibration, and moisture curing protocols.
steps: Site Clearing & Soil Compaction: Strip organic topsoil entirely, expose firm subgrade, and compact using a mechanical plate compactor to achieve at least 95% Proctor density.
Trench Excavation & Depth Verification: Excavate trenches to engineered depth and verify level benchmarks using a laser level or water level.
Sub-Base & Damp-Proof Membrane (DPM): Lay a 75mm blinding layer of crusher dust/sand, compact it, and install a heavy-duty 250-micron polyethylene damp-proof membrane.
Formwork Construction & Bracing: Build rigid formwork using 32mm planks or marine plywood, secured with strongbacks and wooden stakes every 900mm to prevent blowout.
Reinforcement Spacing & Cover Blocks: Position steel rebar grids or mesh using plastic or concrete cover blocks (minimum 50mm clearance) to ensure full steel encapsulation.
Formwork Inspection & Pre-Pour Check: Inspect tie-wires, formwork alignment, squareness, and check that all debris, loose soil, and standing water are cleared.
Mix Design & Slump Verification: Order or mix structural concrete (minimum 25 MPa / 3:2:1 ratio), ensuring a workable slump (75mm - 100mm) without excess water.
Continuous Pouring & Spading: Pour concrete continuously from one corner to prevent cold joints; spade or mechanically vibrate the mix to release trapped air pockets.
Screeding & Surface Finishing: Strike off excess concrete using a straightedge timber screed pulled across form edges, followed by a wood float or steel trowel finish.
Moisture Curing Protocol: Begin curing as soon as the surface hardens by keeping it continuously moist with sprinklers, wet Hessian sacking, or curing compound for at least 7 days.

title: Muffin Tin Ice Cream Station Hack
desc: Create a stable, mess-free ice cream toppings station using an inverted muffin tin to hold small topping cups securely in place.
steps: Gather Supplies: Turn a standard 12-cup metal muffin tin upside down so the raised wells face upward. Collect small paper or silicone baking liners (or small topping cups), assorted toppings in small bowls, an ice cream scoop, and serving spoons.
Secure the Cups: Place the inverted muffin tin flat on your counter or table. Place one small cup or paper liner over each raised well to ensure they fit securely without sliding or tipping.

Fill Toppings: Fill each secured cup with a different ice cream topping (sprinkles, chocolate chips, M&Ms, crushed cookies, gummy bears, nuts, cherries, or hot fudge) for a stable and organized display.
Serve & Enjoy: Set out the ice cream cones and let everyone scoop their favorite toppings with zero spills and total stability—perfect for kids and parties!

title: South African Traditional Foods & Spices Guide
desc: Comprehensive master guide of traditional South African foods and the exact spice blends used to prepare them.
steps: 1. 🌭 Boerewors (Traditional South African Sausage): Coarse salt, black pepper, roasted coriander seeds, cloves, nutmeg, and sometimes allspice.

2. 🥩 Braai Meat / Shisa Nyama (Steaks, Chops, and Chicken): Braai spice blend (coarse sea salt, black pepper, coriander seeds, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika or cayenne pepper, and brown sugar).
3. 🥘 Bobotie (Cape Malay Spiced Mince Bake): Cape Malay curry powder (turmeric, coriander, cumin, ginger), cinnamon, cloves, garlic, and bay leaves.
4. 🥩 Biltong & Droëwors (Cured Meats): Toasted and coarsely cracked coriander seeds, coarse salt, black pepper, brown vinegar, and a pinch of brown sugar or chilli.
5. 🍞 Durban Curry (Mutton, Chicken, or Prawn Bunny Chow): Durban masala (heavy chili powder, cumin, coriander, fenugreek, mustard seeds, and turmeric).
6. 🐟 Cape Pickled Fish (Snoek or Yellowtail): Whole coriander seeds, turmeric, whole cloves, allspice berries, bay leaves, dried chillies, and curry powder.
7. 🍢 Sosaties (Marinated Meat Kebabs): Curry powder, turmeric, garlic, ginger, tamarind or apricot jam (for sweetness), and bay leaves.
8. 🍲 Potjiekos (Traditional Cast-Iron Pot Stew): Whole black peppercorns, bay leaves, garlic, thyme, sweet paprika, and rich beef or vegetable stock.
9. 🍗 Peri-Peri Chicken / Seafood: African bird's eye chillies (peri-peri), garlic, paprika, lemon juice, and salt.
10. 🥫 Chakalaka (Spicy Vegetable Relish): Curry powder, chillies, ginger, garlic, paprika, and white pepper.
11. 🥮 Malva Pudding (Traditional Dessert): Ground cinnamon, nutmeg, and vanilla (served warm with a rich cream/butter sauce).
